chunks.rationale: Issue #408 contract in threadView.test.tsx: jsdom has no ResizeObserver and no layout, so the suite installs a fake observer and overrides scrollHeight/clientHeight/scrollTop. Pinned + growth must set scrollTop to the new scrollHeight; scrolled-up (onScroll, distance > 80px) must leave scrollTop alone. Watch the tests fail first if the observer is missing.
risks: The fake observer fires every watched target at once; it does not prove that a nested load grows a direct child box in a real layout engine.
scrollTop is a writable backing field. A future pin that writes a clamped value (scrollHeight - clientHeight) would fail the first assertion (expects 1400, not 1000).

chunks.rationale: ThreadView adds a ResizeObserver after the existing state-driven pin effect. It observes the scroll body and each direct child, reconnects when `timeline` changes, and only writes scrollTop when stickToBottom.current is set and the view is actually detached (distance > 0). No-ops when ResizeObserver is missing (jsdom).
risks: ResizeObserver on an overflow container reports the viewport box, not scrollHeight. Content growth is detected via the children. A descendant that grows inside a fixed-height / overflow:hidden child would not fire.
A pin that reveals a scrollbar can shrink child width and re-fire the observer. The distance <= 0 guard is what stops a loop.
timeline is memoized on the whole `detail` object, so a new detail identity rebinds observers even when messages are unchanged. Same churn as the existing pin effect.

chunks.rationale: App.tsx now early-returns BuildMismatchScreen when isBuildMismatch(app.status().build.sha, __BUILD_SHA__) is true. The three-pane shell (data-layout=app) is not mounted, so a stale renderer cannot be clicked, typed into, or dismissed past. SHA equality and vite.config.ts stamping are unchanged — no protocolVersion.
risks: appStatus is null until app.status() resolves, so a mismatched window still paints the live app for one IPC round-trip, then swaps to the hard stop. Same timing as the old banner.
useCoder still runs (hooks cannot be skipped), so background IPC/subscriptions continue under the block. User-facing chrome is gone; the stale renderer can still receive pushes.
rendererSha is an optional App prop used as a test seam. Production BootApp does not pass it.

chunks.rationale: BuildMismatchScreen is a full-window alertdialog (title Reload required, existing copy, Restart -> applyUpdate). Banner CSS (mismatchBar) deleted from App.module.css so the old overlay cannot come back by accident.
risks: alertdialog has one control so there is no focus trap. autoFocus on Restart is enough today; a second button would need a trap.
WebTokenGate is also not rendered on mismatch. Intentional: two blocking layers would be worse.

chunks.rationale: test/buildMismatchUi.test.tsx mounts the real App against fakeCoder with a stamped main SHA and the rendererSha seam. It asserts data-layout=app is absent, Restart calls app.applyUpdate, matching/missing SHAs still show the app. Pure isBuildMismatch tests are unchanged.
risks: Node ESM cannot see globalThis.__BUILD_SHA__, so the seam is required. A reviewer deleting the prop without another way to stamp the renderer SHA will make the blocking-state tests unwriteable.

The state-change pin effect is unchanged. This only covers post-paint growth (images, highlight, webfonts). A reviewer who deletes the new effect and keeps the old one would still have a green suite except the two #408 tests.
Issue #184 asked for a protocolVersion handshake. That was deliberately replaced with SHA equality and is NOT reintroduced here — only the hard-stop UX gap is closed.
